questions.q: A force $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=2 \hat{i}+\mathrm{b} \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is applied on a particle and it undergoes a displacement $\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-\hat{k}$. What will be the value of $b$, if work done on the particle is zero.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & w=0 \\ & \therefore \quad \vec{F} \cdot S=0 \\ & (2 \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+\hat{k}) \cdot(\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-\hat{k})=0 \\ & 2-2 b-1=0 \\ & b=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A boy is rolling a $0 . 5kg$~ball on the frictionless floor with the speed of $20\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1} .$~The ball gets deflected by an obstacle on the way. After deflection it moves with $5 %$ of its initial kinetic energy. What is the speed of the ball now?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, $m = 0 . 5kg$ and $u = 20\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$

Initial kinetic energy~\left({k}_{i}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0 . 5 \times 20 \times 20 = 100J$

After deflection it moves with~$5 %$~of~${k}_{i}$

$∴ {k}_{f} = \dfrac{5}{100} \times {k}_{i} ⇒ \dfrac{5}{100} \times 100$

$⇒ {k}_{f} = 5J$

Now, let the final speed be $' v ' \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1},$ then:

${k}_{f} = 5 = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$⇒ v^{2} = 20$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{20} = 4 . 47\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$

$

questions.q:
A body of $m \mathrm{~kg}$ slides from rest along the curve of vertical circle from point $A$ to $B$ in friction less path. The velocity of the body at $B$ is:
$\text { (given, } R=14 \mathrm{~m}, g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \text { and } \sqrt{2}=1.4 \text { ) }$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Apply W.E.T. from A to B $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{mg}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{A}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{mg} \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{2}}+\mathrm{R}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2-0\left\{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}=0 \text { rest }\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{mgR} \frac{(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{gR} \frac{2(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{10 \times 14 \times 2(2.4)}{1.4}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow 21.9=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The ratio of powers of two motors is $\dfrac{3\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}+1}$, that are capable of raising 300 kg water in 5 minutes and 50 kg water in 2 minutes respectively from a well of 100 m deep. The value of $x$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Power of a motor is given by $P = \dfrac{mgh}{t}$.

For the first motor, the power is $P_1 = \dfrac{300 \times g \times 100}{5 \times 60}$.

For the second motor, the power is $P_2 = \dfrac{50 \times g \times 100}{2 \times 60}$.

The ratio of their powers is $\dfrac{P_1}{P_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{300}{5}}{\dfrac{50}{2}} = \dfrac{60}{25} = \dfrac{12}{5}$.

Equating this to the given expression:

$\dfrac{3\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x} + 1} = \dfrac{12}{5}$

$\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x} + 1} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$5\sqrt{x} = 4\sqrt{x} + 4$

$\sqrt{x} = 4 \Rightarrow x = 16$

questions.q: A body of mass $0 . 5kg$ travels on straight line path with velocity $v = \left(3x^{2} + 4\right)ms^{- 1}$. The net work done by the force during its displacement from $x = 0$~to $x = 2m$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $v = 3x^{2} + 4$

Initial and final velocities are~${v}_{i} = 3\left(0\right)2 + 4 = 4ms^{- 1}$

and~${v}_{f} = 3\left(2\right)2 + 4 = 16ms^{- 1}$

From work-energy theorem,

$⇒ \Delta KE = \dfrac{1}{2}m \left({v}_f^{2} - {v}_i^{2}\right)

$⇒ $\Delta$KE = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \left({16}^{2} - {4}^{2}\right)

$⇒ $\Delta$KE = W = 60J$

$

questions.q: A wedge of mass $M = 4m$ lies on a frictionless plane. A particle of mass $m$ approaches the wedge with speed $v .$ There is no friction between the particle and the plane or between the particle and the wedge. The maximum height climbed by the particle on the wedge is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From conservation of linear momentum,

$mv = \left(4m + m\right){v}_{f}$
${v}_{f} = \dfrac{v}{5}$
From conservation of mechanical energy,
$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(4m + m\right){v}_f^{2} + mgh$
$v^{2} = 5{v}_f^{2} + 2gh$
$v^{2} = 5 \times {\left(\dfrac{v}{5}\right)}^{2} + 2gh$
$h = \dfrac{2v^{2}}{5g}$

questions.q: A body of mass $2$ kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force given by $\overset{→}{F} = \left(6t\overset{^}{i} + 6t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)N$. The power developed by the force at the time $t$ is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: $\overset{→}{F} = \left(6t\overset{^}{i} + 6t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)N$

Now, $\overset{→}{F} = m\overset{→}{a} = \left(6t\overset{^}{i} + 6t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{F}m = \left(3t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)$

Hence, velocity $\overset{→}{v} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{t}\overset{→}{a}dt = \dfrac{3t^{2}}{2}\overset{^}{i} +t^{3}\overset{^}{j}$

Required power, $P = \overset{→}{F} . \overset{→}{v} = \left(9t^{3} + 6t^{5}\right)W$

questions.q: A stone of mass $m$, tied to a string is being whirled in a vertical circle with a uniform speed. The tension in the string is
options: minimum when the rope is in the horizontal position.
minimum at the highest position of the circular path.
minimum at the lowest position of the circular path.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the speed is constant, centripetal force required towards the centre of the circle will be same. At the top, direction of gravitational force and tension acting on the object will be same. Therefore, we can write,

$mg + T = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} ⇒ T = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} - mg$.

& Clearly in this case, tension in& the string will be minimum.

questions.q:
Identify the correct statements from the following:

(A) Work done by a man in lifting a bucket out of a well by means of a rope tied to the bucket is negative

(B) Work done by gravitational force in lifting a bucket out of a well by a rope tied to the bucket is negative

(C) Work done by friction on a body sliding down an inclined plane is positive

(D) Work done by an applied force on a body moving on a rough horizontal plane with uniform velocity is& zero

(E) Work done by the air resistance on an oscillating pendulum is& negative

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done is given by,& $W = Fscos\theta$, where~$\theta$& is the angle between the force and the displacement.

case(A): Direction of force and displacement both are in the same direction and hence work done will be positive. Hence, wrong.

case(B): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite& direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, correct.

case(C): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite& direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, wrong.

case(D): Direction of force and displacement both are in the same direction and hence work done will be positive. Hence, wrong.

case(E): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite& direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, correct.

questions.q: An automobile of mass& $m$ accelerates starting from the origin and initially at rest, while the engine supplies constant power $P$. The position is given as a function of time by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$P = const$

$P = {F}_{V} = \dfrac{mv^{2}dv}{dx}$

${∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{P}{m}dx = {∫}_{0}^{v}v^{2}dv$

$\dfrac{Px}{m} = \dfrac{v3}{3}$

\left(\dfrac{3Px}{m}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} = v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

\left(\dfrac{3P}{m}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}{∫}_{0}^{t}dt = {∫}_{0}^{x}x^{- \dfrac{1}{3}}dx$

$⇒ x = \left(\dfrac{8P}{9m}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}t\dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q: A bob of mass $m$ is suspended at a point $O$ by a light string of length $l$ and left to perform vertical motion (circular) as shown in figure. Initially, by applying horizontal velocity $v_0$ at the point ' A ', the string becomes slack when, the bob reaches at the point ' D '. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the bob at the points $B$ and $C$ is ______ -.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{A}}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2+\mathrm{mgh} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}(5 \mathrm{~g} \ell)=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}}^2+\mathrm{mg} \frac{\ell}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{5 \mathrm{mg} \ell}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{mg} \ell}{2}=\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{B}}=2 \mathrm{mg} \ell \\ & \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{C}}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{D}}^2+\mathrm{mg} \frac{\ell}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mg} \ell+\mathrm{mg} \frac{\ell}{2}=\mathrm{mg} \ell \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{C}}}=2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the potential energy between two molecules is given by& $U = \dfrac{A}{r6} + \dfrac{B}{r12},$ then at equilibrium, separation between molecules, and the potential energy are:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$U = \dfrac{A}{r6} + \dfrac{B}{r12}$

$f = - \dfrac{dU}{dr}$

For equilibrium

$f = 0$

so~$r = \left(\dfrac{2B}{A}\right)\dfrac{1}{6}$

Then,~$U = \dfrac{A2}{4B}$

questions.q: Arrange the four graphs in descending order of total work done; where ${W}_{1}, {W}_{2}, {W}_{3}$ and ${W}_{4}$~are the work done corresponding to figure $a, b, c$ and $d$ respectively.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As seen from figure, work done in first graph,& ${W}_{a} = 0$.

Now, work done in figure~$b$,~${W}_{b} = + ve$, and that in figure~$c$,~${W}_{c} = + ve$,~$> {W}_{b}$.

In last graph, work done is~${W}_{d} = - ve$.

So, the descending order of total work done is~

$⇒ {W}_{c} > {W}_{b} > {W}_{a} > {W}_{d}$

$⇒ {W}_{3} > {W}_{2} > {W}_{1} > {W}_{4}$

questions.q: A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time $\mathrm{t}$ is proportional to :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & P=\operatorname{constant} \Rightarrow \mathrm{FV}=\text { constant } \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{m} \frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dt}} \mathrm{V}=\text { constant } \\ & \int_0^{\mathrm{V}} \mathrm{VdV}=(\mathrm{C}) \int_0^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt} \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{2}\right)=\mathrm{Ct} \\ & \mathrm{V} \propto \mathrmt^{1 / 2} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{ds}}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto \mathrmt^{1 / 2} \\ & \int_0^{\mathrm{S}} \mathrm{ds}=\mathrm{K} \int_0^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrmt^{1 / 2} \mathrm{dt} \\ & \mathrm{S}=\mathrm{K} \times \frac{2}{3} \mathrmt^{3 / 2} \\ & \mathrm{~S} \propto \mathrmt^{3 / 2}\end{aligned}\therefore$ displacement is proportional to $(\mathrm{t})^{3 / 2}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $\mathbf{A}$ and the other is labelled as Reason $\mathbf{R}$
Assertion A: In a central force field, the work done is independent of the path chosen.
Reason R: Every force encountered in mechanics does not have an associated potential energy.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are true but $\mathbf{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$
Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are true and $\mathbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assertion is correct as central forces are conservative in nature, i.e. work done is independent of path. Reason is true as some forces in mechanics like, friction are non-conservative because work done depends on path and only conservative forces have an associated potential energy.
Also, reason does not explain assertion.

questions.q: A body of mass $m$ dropped from a height $h$~reaches the ground with a speed of $0 . 8\sqrt{gh} .$& The value of work done& by the air-friction is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${K}_{1} + {U}_{1} = {K}_{2} + {U}_{2} + {W}_{f}$
${W}_{f}:$ work done against friction
$0 + mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + 0 + {W}_{f}$
$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(0 . 64\right)gh + {W}_{f}$
${W}_{f} = 0.68mgh$
Work done by friction ${W}_f^{'} = - {W}_{f} = - 0.68mgh$

questions.q: A block of mass 25 kg is pulled along a horizontal surface at a constant velocity by a force at an angle $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ with the horizontal. The friction coefficient between the block and the surface is 0.25. The work done by the pulling force for a displacement of 5 m of the block is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Block travels with uniform velocity
So $\quad \mathrm{a}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~F} \cos 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=$ friction
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}=\mu\left[\mathrm{mg}-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}\right] \\ & \frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}=0.25\left[25 \times 9.8-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 1.25 \frac{\mathrm{~F}}{\sqrt{2}}=61.25 \\ & \mathrm{~F}=\frac{61.25 \times \sqrt{2}}{1.25}=49 \sqrt{2} \\ & \mathrm{~W}_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathrm{FS} \cos 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \\ &=49 \sqrt{2} \times 5 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=245 \mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A block of mass $10$ kg is moving along $x$-axis under the action of force $F = 5xN$. The work done by the force in moving the block from $x = 2m$ to $4m$ will be _______ $J$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done is& $W = ∫ Fdx$

It is given that

$F = 5xN$

So, work done is~

$W = {∫}_{2}^{4}5xdx = {\dfrac{5x^{2}}{2}}_{2}^{4} ⇒ W = \dfrac{5 ( 16 - 4 )}{2} = 30J$

questions.q: A block moving horizontally on a smooth surface with a speed of $40\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ splits into two equal parts. If one of the parts moves at $60\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ in the same direction, then the fractional~change in the kinetic energy will be $x: 4$~where $x =$& ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$2m \times 40 = 60 \times m + mv$
$V = 20m / s$
Now $\Delta KE = K{E}_{f} - K{E}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}m \times ( 20{)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m \times ( 60{)}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}2m \times ( 40{)}^{2}$
$\Delta KE = \dfrac{1}{2}m ( 800 ) ⇒ K{E}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}2m \times ( 40{)}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m \times 3200$
Fractional change $= \dfrac{\Delta KE}{K{E}_{i}} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

questions.q: A circular table is rotating with an angular velocity of $\omega \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ about its axis (see figure). There is a smooth groove along a radial direction on the table. A steel ball is gently placed at a distance of $1 \mathrm{~m}$ on the groove. All the surfaces are smooth. If the radius of the table is $3 \mathrm{~m}$, the radial velocity of the ball w.r.t. the table at the time ball leaves the table is $x \sqrt{2} \omega \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$, where the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & a_c=\omega^2 x \\ & \frac{v d v}{d x}=\omega^2 x \\ & \int_0^v v d v=\int_1^3 \omega^2 x d x \\ & \frac{v^2}{2}=\omega^2\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right] \\ & \frac{v^2}{2}=\frac{\omega^2}{2}\left[3^2-1^2\right] \\ & v=2 \sqrt{2} \omega \\ & x=2\end{aligned}$

If the radius of the table is $3 \mathrm{~m}$, the radial velocity of the ball w.r.t. the table at the time ball leaves the table is $x \sqrt{2} \omega \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$, where the value of $x$ is _____.

questions.q: To maintain a speed of $80kmh^{- 1}$ by a bus of mass $500$ kg on a plane rough road for $4$ km distance, the work done by the engine of the bus will be _____~$kJ$. [The coefficient of friction between tyre of bus and road is $0 . 04$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given,

$v = 80kmh^{- 1}$

$m = 500kg$

$S = 4km$

$\mu = 0 . 04$

The power~due to friction is~

${P}_{f} = Fv$~where~$F = \mumg$

$= \left(\left(0 . 04\right)\left(500 \times 9 . 8\right) \times 80 \times \dfrac{5}{18}\right)W$

Hence, the work done by the engine in overcoming the friction is

$W = {P}_{f}t = {P}_{f}\dfrac{d}{v}$

$⇒ W = 20 \times 9 . 8 \times 80 \times \dfrac{5}{18} \times \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{3}}{80 \times \dfrac{5}{18}} = 784kJ$

questions.q: A pendulum is suspended by a string of length $250$ cm. The mass of the bob of the pendulum is $200g$. The bob is pulled aside until the string is at $60 °$ with vertical as shown in the figure. After releasing the bob, the maximum velocity attained by the bob will be _____~$ms^{- 1}$. (if $g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Velocity will be maximum at the bottom point when potential energy of the pendulum will be zero(considering bottom point as reference for potential energy).

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = mg\left(l - lcos60 °\right)v = \sqrt{gl} = \sqrt{10 \times 2 . 5} = 5ms^{- 1}$
